title: Aftershock: failover oscillation and aggressive shedding during cross-region surge
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A high-traffic event on 2026-02-27 triggered a partial regional failover that exposed a configuration mismatch between circuit-breaker hysteresis and load-shedding thresholds across regions. Traffic oscillated between primary and secondary regions, causing p99 latency and success-rate SLO misses for a 22-minute window. The incident required an emergency rollback of a circuit-breaker hysteresis change, temporary relaxation of shedding policies, and a coordinated cache-warmup campaign to stabilise tail latency.
timeline: 2026-02-27T14:03Z - First elevated error rates detected on primary region (us-west-2) for model /v1/generate routes.
2026-02-27T14:05Z - Automated regional failover policy started redirecting 30% of new sessions to eu-west-1 as latency crossed the soft-SLO threshold.
2026-02-27T14:07Z - eu-west-1 circuit breakers, configured with more aggressive open thresholds in the recent rollout, began tripping and shedding according to the new profile.
2026-02-27T14:10Z - Observed traffic oscillation: as eu-west-1 shed, traffic remapped back to us-west-2, pushing us-west-2 over higher tail latencies leading to further failover attempts.

2026-02-27T14:25Z - Root-cause narrowing: mismatched hysteresis and lack of KV-cache priming in the receiving region amplified tail latency. Incident commander ordered temporary rollback of hysteresis change (PR #4102) and set shedding thresholds to conservative defaults.
2026-02-27T14:45Z - Cache-warmup job ramped for critical prefixes; traffic smoothing rules applied to routing to stop rapid oscillation.
2026-02-27T15:05Z - Metrics returned within SLO targets; emergency mitigation transitioned to follow-up action plan.
2026-02-27T15:25Z - Incident declared resolved for customer-facing impact; post-incident analysis kicked off.
2026-02-28T09:00Z - Initial notes and evidence collected; task created for deeper root-cause and long-term fixes (this ticket).
2026-03-10T11:30Z - Engineering review with runtime, routing, and infra teams; prioritized action items assigned.
impact: Approximately 22 minutes of customer-visible SLO degradation across two regions. Measured impact: p99 latency increased from 520ms to 1.9s, availability (success_rate) dropped from 99.93% to 98.1% for affected routes. Estimated customer requests impacted: ~7.4k RPS aggregated over the incident window. No data leakage or security incident.
root_cause: A rollout of a circuit-breaker hysteresis tuning (PR #4102) changed the open/close timers and allowed more aggressive opening in eu-west-1. That change was not coupled with coordinated load-shedding and routing policy adjustments nor with a cache-warmup step. When traffic was partially diverted during failover, eu-west-1's unprimed KV caches and aggressive breaker opened repeatedly, shedding load. The routing control plane immediately sent traffic back to us-west-2, creating an oscillation loop that amplified tail latency and triggered further failovers. Lack of cross-region simulation and missing automated canary gating for control-plane config changes allowed the configuration mismatch to reach production.
mitigation: Short-term: rollback of PR #4102, revert eu-west-1 breaker hysteresis to previous values, reduce shedding aggressiveness to default thresholds, and enable temporary traffic smoothing (5s ramp windows). Initiated targeted cache priming for high-volume prefixes and increased short-term autoscaling allowances in eu-west-1. Long-term: multi-region canary for control-plane config changes, add hysteresis and shedding coupling checks to CI, improve runbooks for coordinated rollouts, and extend observability for cross-region hysteresis metrics.
action_items: ENG-87219-A1: Implement multi-region canary gating for routing and circuit-breaker config changes (owner: Marco Chen, due: 2026-03-20, estimate: 5)
ENG-87219-A2: Add CI checks that validate combined hysteresis + shedding policy across region pairs (owner: Sofie Müller, due: 2026-03-18, estimate: 3)

ENG-87219-A3: Extend telemetry: expose 'breaker_hysteresis_state' and 'shedding_rate' cross-region correlation dashboard and add alert for oscillation patterns (owner: Liam O'Connor, due: 2026-03-15, estimate: 3)

ENG-87219-A4: Update routing runbook to include 'micro-ramp' and minimum hold windows to avoid sub-30s oscillations; add explicit checklist for cache warmup before ramping traffic (owner: Diego Alvarez, due: 2026-03-12, estimate: 2)
ENG-87219-A5: Backfill automated regional load tests in staging to cover cache warmup and breaker behavior under asymmetric priming (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-03-28, estimate: 8)
ENG-87219-A6: Create a post-deploy dashboard snapshot in PR templates for any breaker/hysteresis changes that surfaces risk signals (owner: Marco Chen, due: 2026-03-22, estimate: 2)

ENG-87219-A7: Review and harden default shedding policy to include a progressive fallback to queued requests instead of immediate drop for stateful flows (owner: Sofie Müller, due: 2026-04-05, estimate: 5)

ENG-87219-A8: Communicate incident summary and interim mitigations to enterprise customers with Dedicated contracts; schedule customer-specific follow-ups where SLA exposure occurred (owner: Hannah Reed, due: 2026-03-14, estimate: 1)

ENG-87219-A9: Postmortem doc and triage board to be shared with SRE and product leadership; track completion of above items and deliver a 30-day review (owner: Marco Chen, due: 2026-04-26, estimate: 1)
ENG-87219-A10: Add chaos test that intentionally flips breaker hysteresis values across regions to ensure no amplification loops (owner: Diego Alvarez, due: 2026-04-12, estimate: 5)
notes: We observed that KV cache priming latency alone increased p99 by ~200-300ms before breakers started to open. Cache warmup reduced tail by ~650ms within 8 minutes.
The problematic change had been flagged low-risk in the config PR because it passed unit tests and single-region load tests; lack of multi-region gating was the oversight.
Traffic smoothing applied at 5s windows proved effective; we should standardize this as 'micro-ramp' in routing policies.
No customer data was exposed. Impacted customers have been contacted where Dedicated SLAs indicated potential exposure to degraded availability.
